# Social Media Posting

Adapts LinkedIn posts for Mastodon and Bluesky, then schedules them via the Buffer GraphQL API.

## Commands

```bash
npm test                    # Run tests (vitest)
npm run post                # Schedule posts to Buffer queue via API
npm run post -- --now       # Publish posts immediately via API
npm run post -- --dry-run   # Preview API payloads without posting
npm run batch -- --file analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/<name>.json [--dry-run]
                            # Batch-schedule evergreen posts (10:00, 13:30 ET weekdays).
                            # Marks the calendar/quiz seed as each post is accepted; --no-mark opts out.
                            # Paths are cwd-relative: run from the agile-pain-relief-astro repo root.
npm run validate -- --file <path-to-batch.json>
                            # Run batch pre-flight only: no token, no network, no writes. This is the
                            # single implementation of the char-limit/URL rules; skills call it rather
                            # than counting characters themselves. Paths are cwd-relative.
npm run calendar-audit      # Diff the reshare queue vs live blog/glossary; --write refreshes the header
                            # (reads agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/)
npm run reshare-report      # Rank posted queue items by clicks-per-reshare (PostHog archive-reshare
                            # attribution + history.json engagement). Feeds the quarterly queue tune.
                            # Flags: --top N, --json. Run from the agile-pain-relief-astro repo root.
npm run scrape              # Sync LinkedIn, Mastodon and Bluesky engagement metrics from
                            # Buffer to history.json via the GraphQL API (buffer-post/syncMetrics.ts).
                            # Paths are cwd-relative: run from the agile-pain-relief-astro repo root.
                            # Flags: --dry-run (don't write), --weeks N (window, default 6),
                            #   --since YYYY-MM-DD (explicit start, overrides --weeks; for one-off backfills).
                            # Requires the token to have the `insights:read` scope (see below).
```

(The PostHog CSV exporter moved to the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo:
`scripts/posthog-export.ts`, run there as `npm run posthog-export`.)

## Environment Setup

Requires a `.env` file in the project root (gitignored):

```
BUFFER_API_TOKEN=your_token_here
```

(The PostHog exporter that used `POSTHOG_TOKEN` moved to the `agile-pain-relief-astro`
repo; that token now lives in that repo's `.env`.)

Create an API token at Buffer's developer settings. Channel IDs for LinkedIn, Mastodon, and Bluesky are stored as constants in `bufferPost.ts`.

`npm run scrape` reads per-post engagement metrics, which Buffer gates behind the
**`insights:read`** OAuth scope. A `posts:read`/`posts:write` token can create and read
posts but returns `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` for the `metrics` field — re-authorize/create a token
that includes `insights:read`. (Metrics are refreshed by Buffer's daily ingestion job, so
`metricsUpdatedAt` can lag the live network value by ~24h.)

## Project Structure

```
social-media/temp/  # Post content files (created by adapt skill)
  linkedin.txt              # Source post (plain text)
  mastodon.json             # Adapted Mastodon thread: { "parts": ["..."] }
  bluesky.json              # Adapted Bluesky thread: { "parts": ["..."] }
buffer-post/          # Buffer GraphQL API client: scheduling (bufferPost.ts, batchPost.ts),
                      #   standalone pre-flight (validateBatch.ts), content-queue marking
                      #   (sourceMarking.ts), and engagement-metrics sync (syncMetrics.ts +
                      #   pure logic in metricsSync.ts)
reshare-report/       # Reshare performance measurement: pure metrics (reshareMetrics.ts)
                      #   + CLI (reshareReport.ts)
calendar-audit/       # Queue-vs-live-site diff (calendarAudit.mjs)
```

Everything talks to Buffer through its GraphQL API. There is no browser automation: the
Playwright scraper (`buffer-export-via-playwright/`, `npm run export`,
`npm run scrape:playwright`) was deleted on 2026-07-27 once the API-based `npm run scrape`
proved stable, along with its `historyStore.ts` (superseded by `metricsSync.ts`) and the
`playwright` dependency. Recover from git history if ever needed.

Analytics data (history.json, PostHog CSVs, Ahrefs CSVs) lives in the sibling `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo under `analytics/`. The evergreen batch lives there too, at `analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/`: the `<name>.json` batch files (array of `{ linkedin, mastodon, bluesky, url?, image? }`, where `mastodon`/`bluesky` are a single string or an array of thread parts; written by the `evergreen-posting` skill) and `.schedule-state.json` (ET slots used by past batch runs). `npm run batch` reads and writes that directory relative to cwd, so it must be run from the astro repo root.

## Platform Character Limits

- **LinkedIn**: 2000 chars (post will be rejected if over-limit)
- **Mastodon**: 500 chars per part (Buffer limit)
- **Bluesky**: 290 chars per part (Bluesky's hard limit is 300; we leave a 10-char safety margin — posts at 296-300 empirically get rejected)
- URLs count at full length toward limits (Buffer shortens them after posting)

## Key Patterns

- **Links stay in the post body**: the link is left inline in the LinkedIn body, same as Mastodon and Bluesky. There is no first-comment extraction (the older first-comment pattern is retired). In the batch (evergreen) path, when an entry sets a `url` field it is appended to each platform's **last part** (the post itself when single-part, the final reply when threaded). Setting `url` while a body also has an inline URL is a hard pre-flight error.
- **UTM parameters**: Automatically appended to `agilepainrelief.com` URLs per platform (e.g. `?utm_source=mastodon&utm_campaign=archive-reshare`). URLs that already have `utm_` params are skipped.
- **Cover images**: the two paths differ. `npm run post` (`bufferPost.ts`) extracts the `og:image` URL from the linked blog post and passes it to the Buffer API (no download needed — the API accepts URLs directly). `npm run batch` does **not** auto-fetch: `resolveCoverImage` uses the entry's `image` field only, and `""` means no image. Auto-fetch was deliberately left out of the batch path because Buffer's dedup matches shared image assets across posts pointing at the same source page, which evergreen reshares hit constantly — so if images are used here, each entry needs a distinct URL.
- **Threading**: Mastodon and Bluesky multi-part posts use Buffer API's `metadata.mastodon.thread` / `metadata.bluesky.thread` fields. First part is the main `text`, remaining parts go in the thread array. Both entry paths can thread: `social-media-adapt` via the `parts` array in `mastodon.json`/`bluesky.json`, and the batch path via `string | string[]` on `BatchEntry.mastodon`/`.bluesky`. Threading exists mainly so a Bluesky post whose message + link exceeds 290 can keep the message in the root and put the link in a short reply — each part is validated against the full limit independently.
- **Buffer API**: GraphQL API at `https://api.buffer.com`. One `createPost` mutation per channel (3 calls for LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky).
- **This repo owns the rules; the skills own the writing.** Any hard number or checkable rule (character limits, per-network URL counting, posts-per-weekday, UTM format, posted-marker syntax) is encoded here once, with a test, and exposed as an `npm run` command. The authoring skills in `agile-pain-relief-astro/.claude/skills/` describe how to *write* a post and call these commands for anything checkable. When a skill restates a rule as prose, that prose is documentation, not a second implementation — if the two disagree, fix the skill.
- **Source marking** (`sourceMarking.ts`, pure; wired into `batchPost.ts`): when Buffer accepts a post, the scheduler stamps its source. Blog/glossary items are matched to the calendar queue by the `url`'s `collection/slug` (UTM and trailing slashes ignored); quiz posts are matched to a seed block by the entry's `seed` field, an exact substring. Posted markers accumulate dates: `(2026-05-29, 2026-07-27)`, with the legacy `, 3x` shorthand carried forward. Marking is idempotent and refuses to act on an ambiguous or missing match, reporting it in the run summary instead. It writes after each accepted post, so a mid-batch crash leaves the ledger matching what is actually queued. Skipped on `--dry-run` and under `--no-mark`.
- **Reshare measurement** (`reshare-report/`): ranks on **clicks-per-reshare**, never raw sessions. The PostHog entry-path CSV holds overlapping rolling 30-day snapshots, so only the latest snapshot per `(entry_path, utm_source)` is counted. Rows whose `snapshot_date` is the literal `unknown` are **dropped and reported** — string-comparing them would rank `"unknown"` above every real date and hand the series to a row of unknown provenance. Times-reshared is the max of the calendar's posted markers and history.json slug hits, since each ledger is separately incomplete.
- **History management**: `metricsSync.ts` (`mergeMetricsIntoHistory`) merges API-fetched engagement into `history.json`. Matching is three-pass — the platform's own text field, then the linkedin text field, then an exact scheduled-slot match (`dueAt`→ET equals `posted`). The slot pass works because all three channels share one `dueAt` per content piece: LinkedIn is merged first (creating/back-filling the entry and its `posted`), so the Mastodon/Bluesky adaptations land on it even when their adapted text was never stored. Unmatched LinkedIn posts create new entries; unmatched Mastodon/Bluesky (organic native posts) are skipped. Pure functions are tested; I/O and network are separated in `syncMetrics.ts`.
- **Metric vocabulary mapping**: Buffer's API normalizes engagement across networks (`reactions`, `comments`, `reposts`), but `history.json` keeps platform-native names. Mappers translate back: Mastodon `{favorites←reactions, replies←comments, reblogs←reposts}`; Bluesky `{likes←reactions, comments, reposts}`; LinkedIn keeps `{reactions, comments, impressions, reach, engagementRate}` (`engagementRate` stored as an integer `"N%"` string). Change these together with the downstream dashboard if the shapes ever move.

## Content Adaptation

Authoring conventions (character limits, threading, hashtags, URL handling, style) live in the Astro repo at `.claude/skills/_social-posting-conventions.md`, shared by the `social-media-adapt` and `evergreen-posting` skills. This pipeline is the enforcement authority: if a skill disagrees with what the code here actually does, the code wins.

Use the `social-media-adapt` skill to convert a single LinkedIn post to Mastodon/Bluesky format, or `evergreen-posting` to generate a batch from the curated queue in `agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/`.

## Gotchas

- Most scripts use `import.meta.url` to resolve paths from the script's location, not cwd, so they work when run from either this repo or `agile-pain-relief-astro`. **Exception:** `batch` (`batchPost.ts`) resolves both `--file` and the evergreen/state directory relative to **cwd**, so it must be run from the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo root (where `analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/` lives).
- Never shorten URLs in content files — Buffer handles shortening automatically.
- Bluesky is strict on the 300-char limit; posts will be rejected if over.
- Post content goes in `social-media/temp/` (not `content/` or `posts/`).
- `history.json` sorts posts by `posted` date descending (newest first).

## Analytics Data

### PostHog (in `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/posthog/`)

CSV exports from PostHog tracking visitor behavior on agilepainrelief.com. Updated incrementally by `npm run posthog-export` (the exporter now lives in the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo at `scripts/posthog-export.ts`) via the PostHog Insights API (EU endpoint, project 59984). Uses fixed filenames (no date stamps). Three update strategies:

- **Week-keyed (additive by week):** Old weeks preserved, overlapping weeks refreshed, current incomplete week excluded.
  - `export-pageviews-by-week-utm-source-and-pathname.csv` — unique visitors per page per traffic source per week.
  - `export-average-sessions-by-utm-source-by-week.csv` — total sessions and avg session duration per traffic source per week.

- **Rolling snapshots (additive by snapshot date):** Each run appends a new 30-day snapshot with a `snapshot_date` column. Historical snapshots accumulate.
  - `export-bounce-rate-percentage-by-week.csv` — bounced vs. total sessions and bounce rate percentage.
  - `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` — entry paths with UTM source, medium, and campaign.
  - `export-cta-button-clicks-by-url-and-referrer.csv` — CTA button click counts by page URL and referrer (from PostHog TrendsQuery insight).

- **Events (append-only):** New events appended after the latest existing timestamp, up to end of previous day.
  - `export-404-errors.csv` — raw `page_not_found` events with flattened properties.

### Ahrefs (`analytics/Ahrefs/`)

Periodic CSV exports from Ahrefs tracking SEO performance and backlinks for agilepainrelief.com. Files are date-stamped.

- **Organic keywords** — keyword rankings in US search results including: search volume, keyword difficulty, CPC, current/previous position, position change, traffic estimates, SERP features present, and intent classification (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational).
- **Top pages** — pages ranked by organic traffic including: current/previous traffic and traffic value, number of ranking keywords, top keyword and its position, referring domains, and URL rating.
- **Backlinks** — inbound links to the site including: referring page URL and title, domain rating, anchor text and context, link type (text/image), follow/nofollow status, first seen/last seen dates, and lost/discovered status.

## CLAUDE.md Quality Report

### Summary
- Files found: 3 (1 project root, 1 adjacent coupled repo, 1 global)
- Average score: 81/100
- Files needing update: 2

I verified every documented flag and path against the source rather than reading for plausibility. That turned up four factual errors, one of them actively misleading.

---

### 1. `./CLAUDE.md` (social-media-posting, project root) — 137 lines
**Score: 78/100 (Grade: B)**

| Criterion | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Commands/workflows | 18/20 | All 7 commands present; `--now`, `--dry-run`, `--weeks`, `--since` all verified to exist |
| Architecture clarity | 15/20 | Structure block lists a directory this repo doesn't contain |
| Non-obvious patterns | 14/15 | The file's real strength — image dedup, three-pass matching, metric vocabulary |
| Conciseness | 9/15 | Key Patterns bullets have grown into paragraphs; 25 lines duplicate the astro repo |
| Currency | 10/15 | Two path claims are wrong about the current code |
| Actionability | 12/15 | "Run from repo root" contradicts how the scripts actually resolve paths |

**Issues:**

1. **The path-resolution gotcha is inverted** (line 107). It says "Most scripts use `import.meta.url`… **Exception:** `batch`". The reverse is true — only `calendarAudit.mjs` uses `import.meta.url`. `bufferPost.ts`, `syncMetrics.ts`, `batchPost.ts` and `reshareReport.ts` all use cwd-relative `path.resolve()`. A reader following this would run `scrape` and `post` from the wrong directory.

2. **`.env` is cwd-relative and undocumented as such.** `loadEnv()` does `path.resolve(".env")` (`bufferPost.ts:50`). Since `post`/`batch`/`scrape` must run from the astro repo root, the `.env` actually read is *that repo's*. This is why both repos have one — currently unexplained, and it looked like a bug when I hit it earlier.

3. **`social-media/temp/` is listed under this repo's Project Structure but doesn't exist here.** It's resolved cwd-relative (`bufferPost.ts:568`) and lives in the astro repo.

4. **Conciseness**: the Analytics Data section (25 lines) largely restates astro's CLAUDE.md §364-375 and describes CSVs this repo doesn't produce. Only `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` is actually consumed here. Separately, the Key Patterns bullets I added earlier today (source marking, reshare measurement) run 6-7 lines of prose each — too long for this format.

---

### 2. `../agile-pain-relief-astro/CLAUDE.md` — scoped to its social-media sections
**Score: 72/100 (Grade: B-)** *(scoped; I did not audit the other ~380 lines about the Astro site)*

**Issues:**

1. **Cadence is wrong** (line 351): "3 posts/weekday at 10:00, 13:30, 15:30 ET". `slotPlan.mjs` defines two slots, 10:00 and 13:30. This is the same drift I fixed in the skill and vault notes earlier — I missed this copy.
2. **Social commands block (lines 417-424) omits the cwd-sensitive commands**: `batch`, `validate`, `reshare-report`, `calendar-audit`. These are precisely the ones that *must* run from the astro repo root, so their absence from the astro repo's own docs is the costly gap.

**Clean:** no references to the deleted Playwright commands. It correctly defers pipeline behaviour to this repo rather than duplicating it.

---

### 3. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (global) — 25 lines
**Score: 92/100 (Grade: A)** — Two rules, both specific and actionable, including the `min-release-age` vs pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` trap. No changes recommended.

---

### Proposed updates

| # | File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | this repo | Correct the inverted path-resolution gotcha; name which script is the exception | Currently misdirects |
| 2 | this repo | Document that `.env` is read cwd-relative | Explains the two `.env` files |
| 3 | this repo | Move `social-media/temp/` out of the structure block, note it's astro-side | Structure is wrong |
| 4 | this repo | Cut Analytics Data to the one CSV consumed here; link astro's CLAUDE.md | ~20 lines of duplication |
| 5 | this repo | Compress the two long Key Patterns bullets I added today | Conciseness |
| 6 | astro repo | Fix cadence to 2 slots; add the four missing cwd-sensitive commands | Same drift class as before |

Note: #6 touches a file with pre-existing uncommitted changes of yours — I'd edit only those two spots.

content.text: Now #4 — cutting the duplicated Analytics Data section down to what this repo actually consumes:

input.old_string:
## Analytics Data

### PostHog (in `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/posthog/`)

CSV exports from PostHog tracking visitor behavior on agilepainrelief.com. Updated incrementally by `npm run posthog-export` (the exporter now lives in the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo at `scripts/posthog-export.ts`) via the PostHog Insights API (EU endpoint, project 59984). Uses fixed filenames (no date stamps). Three update strategies:

- **Week-keyed (additive by week):** Old weeks preserved, overlapping weeks refreshed, current incomplete week excluded.
  - `export-pageviews-by-week-utm-source-and-pathname.csv` — unique visitors per page per traffic source per week.
  - `export-average-sessions-by-utm-source-by-week.csv` — total sessions and avg session duration per traffic source per week.

- **Rolling snapshots (additive by snapshot date):** Each run appends a new 30-day snapshot with a `snapshot_date` column. Historical snapshots accumulate.
  - `export-bounce-rate-percentage-by-week.csv` — bounced vs. total sessions and bounce rate percentage.
  - `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` — entry paths with UTM source, medium, and campaign.
  - `export-cta-button-clicks-by-url-and-referrer.csv` — CTA button click counts by page URL and referrer (from PostHog TrendsQuery insight).

- **Events (append-only):** New events appended after the latest existing timestamp, up to end of previous day.
  - `export-404-errors.csv` — raw `page_not_found` events with flattened properties.

### Ahrefs (`analytics/Ahrefs/`)

Periodic CSV exports from Ahrefs tracking SEO performance and backlinks for agilepainrelief.com. Files are date-stamped.

- **Organic keywords** — keyword rankings in US search results including: search volume, keyword difficulty, CPC, current/previous position, position change, traffic estimates, SERP features present, and intent classification (informational, commercial, transactional, navigational).
- **Top pages** — pages ranked by organic traffic including: current/previous traffic and traffic value, number of ranking keywords, top keyword and its position, referring domains, and URL rating.
- **Backlinks** — inbound links to the site including: referring page URL and title, domain rating, anchor text and context, link type (text/image), follow/nofollow status, first seen/last seen dates, and lost/discovered status.

content.text: Now #5 — compressing the two over-long bullets I added earlier:

input.old_string:
- **Source marking** (`sourceMarking.ts`, pure; wired into `batchPost.ts`): when Buffer accepts a post, the scheduler stamps its source. Blog/glossary items are matched to the calendar queue by the `url`'s `collection/slug` (UTM and trailing slashes ignored); quiz posts are matched to a seed block by the entry's `seed` field, an exact substring. Posted markers accumulate dates: `(2026-05-29, 2026-07-27)`, with the legacy `, 3x` shorthand carried forward. Marking is idempotent and refuses to act on an ambiguous or missing match, reporting it in the run summary instead. It writes after each accepted post, so a mid-batch crash leaves the ledger matching what is actually queued. Skipped on `--dry-run` and under `--no-mark`.
- **Reshare measurement** (`reshare-report/`): ranks on **clicks-per-reshare**, never raw sessions. ## Environment Setup

Requires a `.env` file (gitignored) containing:

```
BUFFER_API_TOKEN=your_token_here
```

**`.env` is read from cwd, not from this repo** (`loadEnv()` does `path.resolve(".env")`). Since the commands are run from the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo root, that repo's `.env` is the one that matters. Both repos keep a copy; keep the token in sync, or you get "BUFFER_API_TOKEN not set" from the directory you're standing in.

(The PostHog exporter that used `POSTHOG_TOKEN` moved to the `agile-pain-relief-astro`
repo; that token now lives in that repo's `.env`.)

Create an API token at Buffer's developer settings. Channel IDs for LinkedIn, Mastodon, and Bluesky are stored as constants in `bufferPost.ts`.

`npm run scrape` reads per-post engagement metrics, which Buffer gates behind the
**`insights:read`** OAuth scope. A `posts:read`/`posts:write` token can create and read
posts but returns `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` for the `metrics` field — re-authorize/create a token
that includes `insights:read`. (Metrics are refreshed by Buffer's daily ingestion job, so
`metricsUpdatedAt` can lag the live network value by ~24h.)

## Project Structure

```
buffer-post/          # Buffer GraphQL API client: scheduling (bufferPost.ts, batchPost.ts),
                      #   standalone pre-flight (validateBatch.ts), content-queue marking
                      #   (sourceMarking.ts), and engagement-metrics sync (syncMetrics.ts +
                      #   pure logic in metricsSync.ts)
reshare-report/       # Reshare performance measurement: pure metrics (reshareMetrics.ts)
                      #   + CLI (reshareReport.ts)
calendar-audit/       # Queue-vs-live-site diff (calendarAudit.mjs)
```

Everything talks to Buffer through its GraphQL API. There is no browser automation: the
Playwright scraper (`buffer-export-via-playwright/`, `npm run export`,
`npm run scrape:playwright`) was deleted on 2026-07-27 once the API-based `npm run scrape`
proved stable, along with its `historyStore.ts` (superseded by `metricsSync.ts`) and the
`playwright` dependency. Recover from git history if ever needed.

**This repo is code only. Every file it reads and writes lives in the sibling `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo**, resolved from cwd:

```
social-media/temp/          # Single-post content, written by the social-media-adapt skill
  linkedin.txt              #   Source post (plain text)
  mastodon.json             #   Adapted thread: { "parts": ["..."] }
  bluesky.json              #   Adapted thread: { "parts": ["..."] }
social-media/planning/      # Curated reshare queue + quiz seeds (marked by npm run batch)
analytics/history.json      # Permanent post record + engagement
analytics/posthog/          # PostHog CSVs (produced there by npm run posthog-export)
analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/   # Batch JSON + .schedule-state.json

- **UTM parameters**: Automatically appended to `agilepainrelief.com` URLs per platform (e.g. `?utm_source=mastodon&utm_campaign=archive-reshare`). URLs that already have `utm_` params are skipped.
- **Cover images**: the two paths differ. `npm run post` extracts `og:image` from the linked page and passes the URL to the API. `npm run batch` does **not** auto-fetch — `resolveCoverImage` uses the entry's `image` field only, `""` meaning none. That was deliberate: Buffer dedups on shared image assets across posts pointing at the same page, which evergreen reshares hit constantly, so each entry needs a *distinct* URL if images are used at all.
- **Threading**: Mastodon and Bluesky multi-part posts use Buffer API's `metadata.mastodon.thread` / `metadata.bluesky.thread` fields. First part is the main `text`, remaining parts go in the thread array. Both entry paths can thread: `social-media-adapt` via the `parts` array in `mastodon.json`/`bluesky.json`, and the batch path via `string | string[]` on `BatchEntry.mastodon`/`.bluesky`. Threading exists mainly so a Bluesky post whose message + link exceeds 290 can keep the message in the root and put the link in a short reply — each part is validated against the full limit independently.
- **Buffer API**: GraphQL API at `https://api.buffer.com`. One `createPost` mutation per channel (3 calls for LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky).
- **This repo owns the rules; the skills own the writing.** Any hard number or checkable rule (character limits, per-network URL counting, posts-per-weekday, UTM format, posted-marker syntax) is encoded here once, with a test, and exposed as an `npm run` command. The authoring skills in `agile-pain-relief-astro/.claude/skills/` describe how to *write* a post and call these commands for anything checkable. When a skill restates a rule as prose, that prose is documentation, not a second implementation — if the two disagree, fix the skill.
- **Source marking** (`sourceMarking.ts`, pure; wired into `batchPost.ts`): when Buffer accepts a post, the scheduler stamps its source, writing after each post so a mid-batch crash leaves the ledger honest. Blog/glossary match the calendar by the `url`'s `collection/slug`; quiz posts match a seed block by the entry's `seed` substring. Markers accumulate dates `(2026-05-29, 2026-07-27)`, preserving the legacy `, 3x` shorthand. Idempotent; an ambiguous or missing match is reported, never guessed. Skipped on `--dry-run` and `--no-mark`.
- **Reshare measurement** (`reshare-report/`): ranks on **clicks-per-reshare**, never raw sessions. Snapshots overlap, so only the latest per `(entry_path, utm_source)` counts. Rows with `snapshot_date=unknown` are dropped and reported — comparing them as strings ranks `"unknown"` above every real date (this put a bogus row at rank 1 before it was caught). Times-reshared is the max of calendar markers and history.json hits; each ledger is separately incomplete.
- **History management**: `metricsSync.ts` (`mergeMetricsIntoHistory`) merges API-fetched engagement into `history.json`. Matching is three-pass — the platform's own text field, then the linkedin text field, then an exact scheduled-slot match (`dueAt`→ET equals `posted`). The slot pass works because all three channels share one `dueAt` per content piece: LinkedIn is merged first (creating/back-filling the entry and its `posted`), so the Mastodon/Bluesky adaptations land on it even when their adapted text was never stored. Unmatched LinkedIn posts create new entries; unmatched Mastodon/Bluesky (organic native posts) are skipped. Pure functions are tested; I/O and network are separated in `syncMetrics.ts`.
- **Metric vocabulary mapping**: Buffer's API normalizes engagement across networks (`reactions`, `comments`, `reposts`), but `history.json` keeps platform-native names. Mappers translate back: Mastodon `{favorites←reactions, replies←comments, reblogs←reposts}`; Bluesky `{likes←reactions, comments, reposts}`; LinkedIn keeps `{reactions, comments, impressions, reach, engagementRate}` (`engagementRate` stored as an integer `"N%"` string). Change these together with the downstream dashboard if the shapes ever move.

## Content Adaptation

Authoring conventions (character limits, threading, hashtags, URL handling, style) live in the Astro repo at `.claude/skills/_social-posting-conventions.md`, shared by the `social-media-adapt` and `evergreen-posting` skills. This pipeline is the enforcement authority: if a skill disagrees with what the code here actually does, the code wins.

Use the `social-media-adapt` skill to convert a single LinkedIn post to Mastodon/Bluesky format, or `evergreen-posting` to generate a batch from the curated queue in `agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/`.

## Gotchas

- **Almost every script resolves paths relative to cwd, so run them from the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo root.** `post`, `batch`, `validate`, `scrape` and `reshare-report` all use `path.resolve()` against cwd for their inputs and outputs (`analytics/history.json`, `analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/`, `social-media/temp/`, `social-media/planning/`, and `--file`). The data they read and write lives in the astro repo, so running them from here silently targets non-existent paths. **The one exception is `calendar-audit`**, which resolves the astro repo from the script's own location via `import.meta.url` and works from either repo.
- Never shorten URLs in content files — Buffer handles shortening automatically.
- Bluesky is strict on the 300-char limit; posts will be rejected if over.

Never write a one-off character-counting script: a second implementation of these rules is how the numbers below drift out of sync with reality. The limits in this doc are documentation; the code is the check.
22	
23	## Character limits (hard)
24	
25	| Platform | Limit per post/part | URLs |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| LinkedIn | 2000 | counted at full length |
28	| Mastodon | 500 | counted as a fixed 23 |
29	| Bluesky  | **290** | counted at full length |
30	
31	Bluesky's platform hard limit is 300, but the pipeline caps at **290** — posts at 296-300 chars empirically get rejected by Buffer, so we keep a 10-char safety margin. Always validate Bluesky against 290, not 300.
32	
33	The pipeline appends the `url` field to each platform's body — to the **last part**, so on a thread the link lands in the final reply — and the link counts toward that part's limit. **Bluesky and LinkedIn count it at full length** (Buffer no longer shortens by default since 2025-04, and Bluesky's API counts the raw URL); **Mastodon counts every URL as a fixed 23.** So on Bluesky the canonical URL plus its UTM (~100-130 chars) comes out of the 290 budget for whichever part carries it: keep a single-part Bluesky body short (~150), or thread it and let a short final part carry the link.
34	
35	## Threading
36	
37	| Platform | Parts |
38	|---|---|
39	| Mastodon | 1-2 preferred, 3 max, never 4 |
40	| Bluesky  | 2-3 max |
41	
42	Both skills support threading. `social-media-adapt` uses a `parts` array. In `evergreen-posting`'s batch JSON, `mastodon` and `bluesky` accept **either a single string (one post) or an array of strings (a thread)**: `[0]` is the root, the rest become replies. `linkedin` is always a single string.
43	
44	Each part is validated against the full per-platform limit independently, and the `url` link is appended to the **last** part — that is the point of threading: the message keeps its substance in the root post and the link rides in a short reply. Prefer a single post; thread when content + link genuinely won't fit (mostly Bluesky). Never pre-shorten a URL yourself.
45	
46	## Hashtags
47	
48	**Always, on every post:**
49	
50	- `#AIinSoftwareDevelopment`
51	
52	**Add when the topic matches (canonical topic list):**
53	
54	`#Agile` `#Scrum` `#ScrumMaster` `#ProductOwner` `#TechnicalDebt` `#TeamWork` `#Leadership`
55	
56	**Per-platform counts:** LinkedIn 2-4 · Mastodon 2-3 · Bluesky 2. Hashtags go at the end of the final post/part.
57	
58	## Emoji
59	
60	Use emoji on every platform (LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky), lightly.
61	
62	- **1-2 per post.** An opening emoji to catch the eye; an optional second to mark a structural turn (e.g. the constructive pivot after a critique). More than two reads as cluttered.
63	- **Never on a vulnerability beat or a serious moment** (a confession, a burnout point) - it undercuts the weight.
64	- **Bluesky:** emoji count against the 290-char budget, so only spend them when they earn the space.
65	- Why: they add colour to otherwise-uniform body text and pull the eye to a key point or the CTA. That is the mechanism; it does not license overuse.
66	
67	## URLs and links
68	
69	- **The link goes in the post body on every platform, LinkedIn included.** There is no "link in the first comment" — that pattern is retired.
70	- **`evergreen-posting` format:** never inline a URL in the body. Put it in the `url` field; the pipeline places it in each platform's body (in the last part, when that platform is threaded). Inlining a URL *and* setting `url` is a hard pre-flight error. **`social-media-adapt` format:** the URL goes inline in the body (Mastodon and Bluesky always carry the link inline).
71	- **Never shorten URLs.** Buffer shortens them automatically.
72	- **Never pre-fill UTM params.** The pipeline appends per-platform UTM (`?utm_source=...&utm_campaign=archive-reshare`) to `agilepainrelief.com` URLs; pre-filling locks the URL to one platform.
73	- **Cover images:** the two paths differ. `social-media-adapt` (`npm run post`) auto-fetches `og:image` from the linked page. The **batch** path does not scrape anything — it posts whatever URL is in `image`, and `""` means no image. Default to `image: ""`; when images are wanted, give every entry in the batch a **distinct** URL (Buffer dedups on shared image assets and skips the duplicates).
74	
75	## Style
76	
77	- **No em dashes.** Use a colon, comma, semicolon, or restructure. (Project-wide rule.)
78	- **No non-breaking spaces (U+00A0).** ASCII spaces only.
79	- Straight quotes and apostrophes are fine in JSON values.
80	- **Never invent stats.** Every number must trace to a real source (a quiz-hook seed or the linked post).

# Social Posting Conventions (shared reference)

Single source of truth for the two social-posting skills:

- **`evergreen-posting`** — batch JSON array, one set across LinkedIn / Mastodon / Bluesky.

## Character limits (hard)

| Platform | Limit per post/part | URLs |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | 2000 | counted at full length |
| Mastodon | 500 | counted as a fixed 23 |
| Bluesky  | **290** | counted at full length |

Bluesky's platform hard limit is 300, but the pipeline caps at **290** — posts at 296-300 chars empirically get rejected by Buffer, so we keep a 10-char safety margin. Always validate Bluesky against 290, not 300.

The pipeline appends the `url` field to each platform's body — to the **last part**, so on a thread the link lands in the final reply — and the link counts toward that part's limit. **Bluesky and LinkedIn count it at full length** (Buffer no longer shortens by default since 2025-04, and Bluesky's API counts the raw URL); **Mastodon counts every URL as a fixed 23.** So on Bluesky the canonical URL plus its UTM (~100-130 chars) comes out of the 290 budget for whichever part carries it: keep a single-part Bluesky body short (~150), or thread it and let a short final part carry the link.

## Threading

| Platform | Parts |
|---|---|
| Mastodon | 1-2 preferred, 3 max, never 4 |
| Bluesky  | 2-3 max |

Both skills support threading. `social-media-adapt` uses a `parts` array. In `evergreen-posting`'s batch JSON, `mastodon` and `bluesky` accept **either a single string (one post) or an array of strings (a thread)**: `[0]` is the root, the rest become replies. `linkedin` is always a single string.

Each part is validated against the full per-platform limit independently, and the `url` link is appended to the **last** part — that is the point of threading: the message keeps its substance in the root post and the link rides in a short reply. Prefer a single post; thread when content + link genuinely won't fit (mostly Bluesky). Never pre-shorten a URL yourself.

## Hashtags

**Always, on every post:**

- `#AIinSoftwareDevelopment`

**Add when the topic matches (canonical topic list):**

`#Agile` `#Scrum` `#ScrumMaster` `#ProductOwner` `#TechnicalDebt` `#TeamWork` `#Leadership`

**Per-platform counts:** LinkedIn 2-4 · Mastodon 2-3 · Bluesky 2. Hashtags go at the end of the final post/part.

## Emoji

Use emoji on every platform (LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky), lightly.

- **1-2 per post.** An opening emoji to catch the eye; an optional second to mark a structural turn (e.g. the constructive pivot after a critique). More than two reads as cluttered.
- **Never on a vulnerability beat or a serious moment** (a confession, a burnout point) - it undercuts the weight.
- **Bluesky:** emoji count against the 290-char budget, so only spend them when they earn the space.
- Why: they add colour to otherwise-uniform body text and pull the eye to a key point or the CTA. That is the mechanism; it does not license overuse.

## URLs and links

- **The link goes in the post body on every platform, LinkedIn included.** There is no "link in the first comment" — that pattern is retired.
- **`evergreen-posting` format:** never inline a URL in the body. Put it in the `url` field; the pipeline places it in each platform's body (in the last part, when that platform is threaded). Inlining a URL *and* setting `url` is a hard pre-flight error. **`social-media-adapt` format:** the URL goes inline in the body (Mastodon and Bluesky always carry the link inline).
- **Never shorten URLs.** Buffer shortens them automatically.
- **Never pre-fill UTM params.** The pipeline appends per-platform UTM (`?utm_source=...&utm_campaign=archive-reshare`) to `agilepainrelief.com` URLs; pre-filling locks the URL to one platform.
- **Cover images:** the two paths differ. `social-media-adapt` (`npm run post`) auto-fetches `og:image` from the linked page. The **batch** path does not scrape anything — it posts whatever URL is in `image`, and `""` means no image. Default to `image: ""`; when images are wanted, give every entry in the batch a **distinct** URL (Buffer dedups on shared image assets and skips the duplicates).

## Style

- **No em dashes.** Use a colon, comma, semicolon, or restructure. (Project-wide rule.)
- **No non-breaking spaces (U+00A0).** ASCII spaces only.
- Straight quotes and apostrophes are fine in JSON values.
- **Never invent stats.** Every number must trace to a real source (a quiz-hook seed or the linked post).

lastPrompt: Are the .claude/skills/_social-posting-conventions.md in the Astro repo still relevant?

content.text:
Yes — but it's now doing two jobs, and only one of them belongs in a document. I checked each section against what the code actually enforces.

## Breakdown

**Documentation of code-enforced rules (~40%)** — character limits, per-platform URL counting, the 290 margin, the inline-URL-plus-`url` conflict. `npm run validate` enforces all of these.

This is *not* dead weight, despite being redundant. There's a real difference between a rule you check afterwards and a budget you must design toward. The model needs to know Bluesky's link costs ~100-130 chars *while* condensing, not just get rejected after. Keep it — it's correctly framed now as "the limits here are documentation; the code is the check."

**Genuine judgement (~35%)** — emoji restraint and when to skip them, tone per platform, "never invent stats", hashtag *vocabulary* (which tags fit which topic), when to thread rather than gut a message. None of this is mechanizable. This is the doc's real reason to exist.

**Checkable rules that nothing checks (~25%)** — and this is the part that undercuts it:

| Rule | Stated in the doc | Enforced |
|---|---|---|
| No em dashes | yes | **no** |
| No U+00A0 | yes | **no** |
| Mastodon ≤3 parts, Bluesky ≤3 | yes | **no** |
| Hashtag counts (LI 2-4, MS 2-3, BS 2) | yes | **no** |
| `#AIinSoftwareDevelopment` on every post | yes | **no** |
| Distinct image URL per batch entry | yes | **no** |
| Never pre-fill UTM | yes | silently skipped, not an error |

I grepped `buffer-post/` for all of these — no matches outside code comments. Every one is currently enforced by the model remembering to follow prose, which is precisely the failure mode this whole session was about.

## The sharpest one

**"No em dashes"** is the rule an LLM is most likely to break by default, it's a one-line regex to check, and nothing checks it. Same for U+00A0, which is invisible in review and would ship straight to Buffer. Those two are the strongest candidates to move into `validate` — a post with an em dash is currently caught only if you happen to notice it.

## So: relevant, but it should get smaller

By the ownership rule we set today, that 25% should move into `npm run validate` and come out of the doc, leaving it as what its frontmatter already claims to be: the authoring reference. That would be roughly a 40-line addition to `validateBatch.ts` plus tests, and it'd shrink the conventions doc to limits-as-budget plus judgement.

One caveat if we do it: the hashtag and thread-count rules are *preferences* ("1-2 preferred, 3 max"), not hard limits like 290. Those want to be warnings that don't fail the run, unlike em dashes and U+00A0, which should be hard errors. Worth splitting the severity rather than making everything fatal.

Want me to codify that 25%?

# Social Posting Conventions (shared reference)

Authoring guidance for the two social-posting skills:

- **`evergreen-posting`** — batch JSON array, one set across LinkedIn / Mastodon / Bluesky.
- **`social-media-adapt`** — a single LinkedIn post adapted into Mastodon / Bluesky threaded JSON.

## The rules are in code, not in this doc

Run `npm run validate` from the Astro repo root. It is the same pre-flight `npm run batch` and `npm run post` run, with no token and no network call:

```bash
npm run validate                                    # single-post path: social-media/temp/
npm run validate -- --file analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/FILE.json   # batch
```

**Errors** (block posting): over character limit, em dash, non-breaking space, 4+ thread parts, a `url` or inline link with `utm_` already set, an inline URL when `url` is also set, a duplicate image URL within a batch, blank parts.

**Warnings** (reported, never blocking): 3-part Mastodon thread, adapted files older than `linkedin.txt`.

Never hand-count characters and never write a one-off checking script. A second implementation of these rules is how they drift apart. What follows is what the checker *cannot* decide for you.

## Budgets to write within

You still need the numbers while drafting, because condensing is your job and rejection after the fact is too late:

| Platform | Limit per post/part | How URLs count |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | 2000 | full length |
| Mastodon | 500 | fixed 23 |
| Bluesky  | **290** | full length |

Bluesky's platform limit is 300; the pipeline caps at 290 because posts at 296-300 empirically get rejected.

**The link is appended to the last part and counts against it.** On Bluesky a canonical URL plus its UTM runs ~100-130 characters, so either keep a single-part Bluesky body near **150**, or thread it and let a short final part carry the link. LinkedIn and Mastodon have room to spare.

## Threading

| Platform | Parts |
|---|---|
| Mastodon | 1-2 preferred, 3 max |
| Bluesky  | 2-3 max |

`social-media-adapt` uses a `parts` array; in `evergreen-posting`'s batch JSON, `mastodon` and `bluesky` take either a single string or an array (`[0]` is the root). `linkedin` is always a single string.

**Prefer a single post.** Thread when content plus link genuinely won't fit — that is the whole point: the message keeps its substance in the root and the link rides in a short reply. Each part is validated against the full limit independently.

## Judgement calls the checker won't make

### Hashtags

`#AIinSoftwareDevelopment` is the house tag. Topic tags when they genuinely fit: `#Agile` `#Scrum` `#ScrumMaster` `#ProductOwner` `#TechnicalDebt` `#TeamWork` `#Leadership`. `#BuildInPublic` and `#ProductCamp` also see regular use.

Counts are **not** enforced, deliberately. Recent practice runs leaner than any written rule (LinkedIn averages under 1 tag, and roughly half of Bluesky posts carry none), and on Bluesky a tag costs characters the message usually needs more. Use them where they earn their place; put them at the end of the final part.

### Emoji

Use them on every platform, lightly.

- **1-2 per post.** An opening emoji to catch the eye; an optional second to mark a structural turn. More reads as cluttered.
- **Never on a vulnerability beat or a serious moment** (a confession, a burnout point): it undercuts the weight.
- **Bluesky:** they cost characters, so only spend them when they earn the space.

### Sourcing

**Never invent stats.** Every number must trace to a real source: a quiz-hook seed, or the post being linked.

### Tone

Mastodon is community-focused and less corporate than LinkedIn; it rewards technical accuracy and cited sources. Bluesky wants brevity and directness. LinkedIn leads with the data point or the provocative claim, never "check out my blog".

## URLs and links

- **The link goes in the post body on every platform, LinkedIn included.** There is no "link in the first comment"; that pattern is retired.
- **`evergreen-posting`:** never inline a URL. Put it in the `url` field and the pipeline places it per platform. **`social-media-adapt`:** the URL goes inline in the body.
- **Never shorten a URL, and never pre-fill UTM.** The pipeline appends `?utm_source=...&utm_campaign=archive-reshare` per platform; pre-filling locks every platform to one source (and is now a hard error).
- **Cover images:** `social-media-adapt` (`npm run post`) auto-fetches `og:image`. The **batch** path does not scrape — it posts whatever is in `image`, and `""` means none. Default to `""`; if you do use images, every entry in the batch needs a **distinct** URL, because Buffer dedups on shared image assets and silently skips the repeat.

## Style

- **No em dashes** and **no non-breaking spaces.** Both are hard errors now, so `npm run validate` will catch them, but write without them in the first place: use a colon, comma, semicolon, or restructure.
- Straight quotes and apostrophes are fine in JSON values.

| Platform | Limit per post/part | URLs |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | 2000 | counted at full length |
| Mastodon | 500 | counted as a fixed 23 |
| Bluesky  | **290** | counted at full length |

| Platform | Parts |
|---|---|

- `#AIinSoftwareDevelopment`

Use emoji on every platform (LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky), lightly.

- **1-2 per post.** An opening emoji to catch the eye; an optional second to mark a structural turn (e.g. the constructive pivot after a critique). More than two reads as cluttered.
- **Never on a vulnerability beat or a serious moment** (a confession, a burnout point) - it undercuts the weight.
- **Bluesky:** emoji count against the 290-char budget, so only spend them when they earn the space.
- Why: they add colour to otherwise-uniform body text and pull the eye to a key point or the CTA. That is the mechanism; it does not license overuse.

## URLs and links

- **The link goes in the post body on every platform, LinkedIn included.** There is no "link in the first comment" — that pattern is retired.
- **`evergreen-posting` format:** never inline a URL in the body. Put it in the `url` field; the pipeline places it in each platform's body (in the last part, when that platform is threaded). Inlining a URL *and* setting `url` is a hard pre-flight error. **`social-media-adapt` format:** the URL goes inline in the body (Mastodon and Bluesky always carry the link inline).
- **Never shorten URLs.** Buffer shortens them automatically.
- **Never pre-fill UTM params.** The pipeline appends per-platform UTM (`?utm_source=...&utm_campaign=archive-reshare`) to `agilepainrelief.com` URLs; pre-filling locks the URL to one platform.
- **Cover images:** the two paths differ. `social-media-adapt` (`npm run post`) auto-fetches `og:image` from the linked page. The **batch** path does not scrape anything — it posts whatever URL is in `image`, and `""` means no image. Default to `image: ""`; when images are wanted, give every entry in the batch a **distinct** URL (Buffer dedups on shared image assets and skips the duplicates).

## Style

- **No em dashes.** Use a colon, comma, semicolon, or restructure. (Project-wide rule.)
- **No non-breaking spaces (U+00A0).** ASCII spaces only.
- Straight quotes and apostrophes are fine in JSON values.
- **Never invent stats.** Every number must trace to a real source (a quiz-hook seed or the linked post).

---
name: social-media-adapt
description: Adapt LinkedIn posts to Mastodon and Bluesky formats with platform-specific character limits, thread formatting, and JSON structure. Use when Claude needs to convert LinkedIn content to other social platforms, create threaded posts, or adapt content for different character limits (Mastodon 500 chars, Bluesky 290 chars).
---

# Social Media Post Adaptation

Adapt LinkedIn posts to Mastodon and Bluesky with proper character limits, thread formatting, and JSON structure.

> **Read [`_social-posting-conventions.md`](../_social-posting-conventions.md) first.** It is the single source of truth for character limits, threading, the hashtag list, URL handling, and style. This skill only adds adaptation-specific guidance on top.

## File Locations

- **Source**: `social-media/temp/linkedin.txt` (plain text)
- **Mastodon Output**: `social-media/temp/mastodon.json` (JSON with parts array)
- **Bluesky Output**: `social-media/temp/bluesky.json` (JSON with parts array)

## JSON Structure

Both platforms use identical structure:

```json
{
  "parts": [
    "First post in thread...",
    "Second post in thread...",
    "Third post in thread..."
  ]
}
```

## Platform Requirements

### Mastodon

**Character Limit**: 500 characters per post (Buffer limit)

**Thread Length**: 1-2 parts preferred, 3 max
- **Single post is the default**: Prefer one tight, well-crafted post over a thread. 500 characters is enough to make a strong point with a link.
- Two-part: Use when the content genuinely needs a setup + payoff that won't fit in one post.
- Three-part: Only for complex, evidence-heavy topics. Avoid if possible.
- **Never use 4 parts.** If you're reaching for a 4th part, tighten the earlier parts instead.

**Thread Strategy** (when threading is necessary):
1. Part 1: Hook + main point
2. Part 2: Evidence or CTA + link

**Tone**: Community-focused, less corporate than LinkedIn

**Hashtags**: 2-3 tags from Standard Hashtags list (the 2 standard + 0-1 topic tag)

**Audience Values**:
- Technical accuracy
- Cited sources
- Open source tools
- Community engagement over personal branding

### Bluesky

**Character Limit**: 290 characters per part (300 hard limit, 10-char safety margin - Buffer rejects posts at 296-300)

**Thread Length**: 2-3 parts maximum
- Aim for conciseness
- Bluesky threads should be shorter than Mastodon

**Thread Strategy**:
1. Part 1: Hook + problem (< 290 chars)
2. Part 2: Key evidence/insight (< 290 chars)
3. Part 3: CTA + link (< 290 chars)

**Tone**: Twitter-like brevity + Mastodon-like authenticity

**Hashtags**: 2 standard tags from Standard Hashtags list (add a topic tag only if space permits)

**Audience Values**:
- Concise, punchy writing
- Direct communication
- Technical credibility
- Authentic conversation

## Adaptation Guidelines

### From LinkedIn to Mastodon

1. **Maintain Core Message**: Keep key argument and evidence
2. **Adjust Tone**: More conversational, less corporate
3. **Preserve Attribution**: Keep research citations (e.g., "SmartBear research")
4. **Use Standard Hashtags**: Always include the 2 standard tags + 0-1 topic tag from the list
5. **Thread Strategically**: Break at natural paragraph boundaries

### From LinkedIn to Bluesky

1. **Tighten Everything**: Aggressive condensing required
2. **Punchy Opening**: First line must grab attention
3. **Preserve Core Data**: Keep key numbers/research but condense
4. **Use Standard Hashtags**: Always include the 2 standard tags; add a topic tag only if space permits
5. **Break at Sentences**: Natural sentence boundaries for parts

## Condensing Techniques for Bluesky

1. **Remove qualifiers**: "very", "really", "quite"
2. **Use abbreviations**: "AI" not "Artificial Intelligence"
3. **Cut redundancy**: "free webinar" not "free webinar event"
4. **Shorter citations**: "SmartBear research" not "Research by SmartBear"
5. **Combine sentences**: Use semicolons or restructure (no em dashes)
6. **Drop obvious words**: "generated code" → "code generated"

**Mental check**: ~48 words ≈ 290 characters (the Bluesky cap)

## Standard Hashtags

See [`_social-posting-conventions.md`](../_social-posting-conventions.md) for the canonical list. Always include `#AIinSoftwareDevelopment`; add topic tags (`#Agile` `#Scrum` `#ScrumMaster` `#ProductOwner` `#TechnicalDebt` `#TeamWork` `#Leadership`) when relevant to the topic. Platform counts: LinkedIn 2-4, Mastodon 2-3, Bluesky 2. Always place hashtags at the end of the final post/part.

## Universal Rules

### URLs
- **NEVER shorten URLs** - Buffer handles link shortening automatically
- Always use full URLs as provided
- URLs count toward character limits
- **Link in the post body on every platform**: the URL goes directly in the post content for LinkedIn, Mastodon, and Bluesky alike. There is no "link in the first comment" pattern any more. If a source LinkedIn post still says "(link in the comments)", restore the actual URL inline.

### Formatting
- Use line breaks for readability
- Include links in final post of thread
- Hashtags at end of final post
- Emoji: 1-2 per post on any platform (see `_social-posting-conventions.md`); skip on serious or vulnerability beats; on Bluesky they count toward the 290-char limit

### Thread Flow
- Each part should be self-contained
- Parts should flow naturally to next
- Break at paragraph/sentence boundaries

## Workflow

1. Read `social-media/temp/linkedin.txt`
2. Create Mastodon version:
   - Adapt content for 500-char limit
   - **Default to a single post.** Only thread if the content truly can't fit in one tight post.
   - Structure as 1-2 parts preferred, 3 max
   - Write to `social-media/temp/mastodon.json`
3. Create Bluesky version:
   - Aggressively condense content
   - Structure as 2-3 part thread
   - **Verify each part < 290 chars**
   - Write to `social-media/temp/bluesky.json`

## Verification

```bash
npm run validate
```

Run from the Astro repo root, after writing both JSON files. It reads `social-media/temp/`, applies UTM exactly as `npm run post` does, and checks character limits (Bluesky at 290, Mastodon URLs at a fixed 23), em dashes, non-breaking spaces, thread length, and pre-filled UTM. It also warns if the adapted files are older than `linkedin.txt`.

**Do not count characters by hand.** The limits in this file are budgets to write within; the command is the check.


## Example: AI Code Generation Post

### LinkedIn (Original)
```
GenAI is making some things easier (i.e. code generation), but what are the costs and tradeoffs? How is it affecting our work?

We're generating more code, but we're also generating more technical debt. When we 10x code volume but 20x the defects, we're not winning, we're compounding our problems.

Here's why this matters: We're spending more time reviewing AI-generated code, which increases our Cognitive Load. Research by SmartBear (studying code reviews at Cisco) shows we can effectively review 200-400 lines of code in one sitting, sustained for 30-60 minutes, and that assumes we understand the system well.

When tools like Claude Code or GitHub Copilot generate 1000 lines of code in a 20-minute stretch, we simply can't review it effectively. We don't have the cognitive capacity, and we often don't understand the generated system well enough.

Meanwhile, the more we rely on these tools, the more our fundamental skills atrophy.

These are just some of the tradeoffs we'll explore in my free webinar: "Where is AI Taking Software Development?"

No hype. I won't promise AGI is coming. Instead, we'll focus on the practical question: How is our work actually changing, and what can we do about it?

https://agilepainrelief.com/where-is-ai-taking-software-development/

#AI #AIinSoftwareDevelopment
```

### Mastodon (2-part thread, 500 char limit)
```json
{
  "parts": [
    "GenAI makes code generation easier, but at what cost?\n\nWe're generating more code AND more technical debt. When we 10x code volume but 20x defects, we're compounding problems. SmartBear research shows we can review 200-400 lines in one sitting. When Copilot generates 1000 lines in 20 min, we can't review it. And our skills atrophy the more we rely on these tools.",
    "Exploring these tradeoffs in my free webinar: \"Where is AI Taking Software Development?\"\n\nNo hype. No AGI promises. Just: How is our work changing, and what can we do about it?\n\nhttps://agilepainrelief.com/where-is-ai-taking-software-development/\n\n#AI #AIinSoftwareDevelopment"
  ]
}
```

### Bluesky (3-part thread, 290 char limit)
```json
{
  "parts": [
    "GenAI is making code generation easier, but at what cost?\n\nWe're generating more code AND more technical debt. When we 10x code volume but 20x defects, we're not winning, we're compounding problems.",
    "The issue: AI-generated code increases review time and Cognitive Load. SmartBear research shows we can review 200-400 lines effectively in one sitting (30-60 min), assuming we know the system.\n\nClaude Code or Copilot generating 1000 lines in 20 min? We can't review it properly.",
    "Plus our skills atrophy the more we rely on these tools.\n\nFree webinar exploring these tradeoffs: \"Where is AI Taking Software Development?\"\n\nNo hype, just practical answers.\n\nhttps://agilepainrelief.com/where-is-ai-taking-software-development/"
  ]
}
```

## Platform Comparison

| Aspect | Mastodon | Bluesky |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Char limit | 500 | 290 |
| Thread length | 1-2 preferred, 3 max | 2-3 max |
| Tone | Community-focused | Individual voice, punchy |
| Verbosity | Tight single posts preferred | Must be concise |

Structure is always `{ "parts": ["..."] }` — one element for a single post, more for a thread.

1	# Social Media Posting
2	
3	Adapts LinkedIn posts for Mastodon and Bluesky, then schedules them via the Buffer GraphQL API.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	npm test                    # Run tests (vitest)
9	npm run post                # Schedule posts to Buffer queue via API
10	npm run post -- --now       # Publish posts immediately via API
11	npm run post -- --dry-run   # Preview API payloads without posting
12	npm run batch -- --file analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/<name>.json [--dry-run]
13	                            # Batch-schedule evergreen posts (10:00, 13:30 ET weekdays).
14	                            # Marks the calendar/quiz seed as each post is accepted; --no-mark opts out.
15	                            # Paths are cwd-relative: run from the agile-pain-relief-astro repo root.
16	npm run validate            # Pre-flight social-media/temp/ (the single-post path)
17	npm run validate -- --file <path-to-batch.json>
18	                            # Pre-flight an evergreen batch. Either form: no token, no network,
19	                            # no writes. The single implementation of the char-limit, style and
20	                            # URL rules; skills call it rather than counting characters.
21	npm run calendar-audit      # Diff the reshare queue vs live blog/glossary; --write refreshes the header
22	                            # (reads agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/)
23	npm run reshare-report      # Rank posted queue items by clicks-per-reshare (PostHog archive-reshare
24	                            # attribution + history.json engagement). Feeds the quarterly queue tune.
25	                            # Flags: --top N, --json. Run from the agile-pain-relief-astro repo root.
26	npm run scrape              # Sync LinkedIn, Mastodon and Bluesky engagement metrics from
27	                            # Buffer to history.json via the GraphQL API (buffer-post/syncMetrics.ts).
28	                            # Paths are cwd-relative: run from the agile-pain-relief-astro repo root.
29	                            # Flags: --dry-run (don't write), --weeks N (window, default 6),
30	                            #   --since YYYY-MM-DD (explicit start, overrides --weeks; for one-off backfills).
31	                            # Requires the token to have the `insights:read` scope (see below).
32	```
33	
34	(The PostHog CSV exporter moved to the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo:
35	`scripts/posthog-export.ts`, run there as `npm run posthog-export`.)
36	
37	## Environment Setup
38	
39	Requires a `.env` file (gitignored) containing:
40	
41	```
42	BUFFER_API_TOKEN=your_token_here
43	```
44	
45	**`.env` is read from cwd, not from this repo** (`loadEnv()` does `path.resolve(".env")`). Since the commands are run from the `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo root, that repo's `.env` is the one that matters. Both repos keep a copy; keep the token in sync, or you get "BUFFER_API_TOKEN not set" from the directory you're standing in.
46	
47	(The PostHog exporter that used `POSTHOG_TOKEN` moved to the `agile-pain-relief-astro`
48	repo; that token now lives in that repo's `.env`.)
49	
50	Create an API token at Buffer's developer settings. Channel IDs for LinkedIn, Mastodon, and Bluesky are stored as constants in `bufferPost.ts`.
51	
52	`npm run scrape` reads per-post engagement metrics, which Buffer gates behind the
53	**`insights:read`** OAuth scope. A `posts:read`/`posts:write` token can create and read
54	posts but returns `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` for the `metrics` field — re-authorize/create a token
55	that includes `insights:read`. (Metrics are refreshed by Buffer's daily ingestion job, so
56	`metricsUpdatedAt` can lag the live network value by ~24h.)
57	
58	## Project Structure
59	
60	```
61	buffer-post/          # Buffer GraphQL API client: scheduling (bufferPost.ts, batchPost.ts),
62	                      #   standalone pre-flight (validateBatch.ts), content-queue marking
63	                      #   (sourceMarking.ts), and engagement-metrics sync (syncMetrics.ts +
64	                      #   pure logic in metricsSync.ts)
65	reshare-report/       # Reshare performance measurement: pure metrics (reshareMetrics.ts)
66	                      #   + CLI (reshareReport.ts)
67	calendar-audit/       # Queue-vs-live-site diff (calendarAudit.mjs)
68	```
69	
70	Everything talks to Buffer through its GraphQL API. There is no browser automation: the
71	Playwright scraper (`buffer-export-via-playwright/`, `npm run export`,
72	`npm run scrape:playwright`) was deleted on 2026-07-27 once the API-based `npm run scrape`
73	proved stable, along with its `historyStore.ts` (superseded by `metricsSync.ts`) and the
74	`playwright` dependency. Recover from git history if ever needed.
75	
76	**This repo is code only. Every file it reads and writes lives in the sibling `agile-pain-relief-astro` repo**, resolved from cwd:
77	
78	```
79	social-media/temp/          # Single-post content, written by the social-media-adapt skill
80	  linkedin.txt              #   Source post (plain text)
81	  mastodon.json             #   Adapted thread: { "parts": ["..."] }
82	  bluesky.json              #   Adapted thread: { "parts": ["..."] }
83	social-media/planning/      # Curated reshare queue + quiz seeds (marked by npm run batch)
84	analytics/history.json      # Permanent post record + engagement
85	analytics/posthog/          # PostHog CSVs (produced there by npm run posthog-export)
86	analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/   # Batch JSON + .schedule-state.json
87	```
88	
89	A batch file is an array of `{ linkedin, mastodon, bluesky, url?, image?, seed? }`, where `mastodon`/`bluesky` are a single string or an array of thread parts, and `seed` (quiz entries only) is the substring used to mark the source seed block. `.schedule-state.json` alongside it caches ET slots used by past runs.
90	
91	## Platform Character Limits
92	
93	- **LinkedIn**: 2000 chars (post will be rejected if over-limit)
94	- **Mastodon**: 500 chars per part (Buffer limit)
95	- **Bluesky**: 290 chars per part (Bluesky's hard limit is 300; we leave a 10-char safety margin — posts at 296-300 empirically get rejected)
96	- URLs count at full length toward limits (Buffer shortens them after posting)
97	
98	## Key Patterns
99	
100	- **Links stay in the post body**: the link is left inline in the LinkedIn body, same as Mastodon and Bluesky. There is no first-comment extraction (the older first-comment pattern is retired). In the batch (evergreen) path, when an entry sets a `url` field it is appended to each platform's **last part** (the post itself when single-part, the final reply when threaded). Setting `url` while a body also has an inline URL is a hard pre-flight error.
101	- **UTM parameters**: Automatically appended to `agilepainrelief.com` URLs per platform (e.g. `?utm_source=mastodon&utm_campaign=archive-reshare`). URLs that already have `utm_` params are skipped.
102	- **Cover images**: the two paths differ. `npm run post` extracts `og:image` from the linked page and passes the URL to the API. `npm run batch` does **not** auto-fetch — `resolveCoverImage` uses the entry's `image` field only, `""` meaning none. That was deliberate: Buffer dedups on shared image assets across posts pointing at the same page, which evergreen reshares hit constantly, so each entry needs a *distinct* URL if images are used at all.
103	- **Threading**: Mastodon and Bluesky multi-part posts use Buffer API's `metadata.mastodon.thread` / `metadata.bluesky.thread` fields. First part is the main `text`, remaining parts go in the thread array. Both entry paths can thread: `social-media-adapt` via the `parts` array in `mastodon.json`/`bluesky.json`, and the batch path via `string | string[]` on `BatchEntry.mastodon`/`.bluesky`. Threading exists mainly so a Bluesky post whose message + link exceeds 290 can keep the message in the root and put the link in a short reply — each part is validated against the full limit independently.
104	- **Buffer API**: GraphQL API at `https://api.buffer.com`. One `createPost` mutation per channel (3 calls for LinkedIn, Mastodon, Bluesky).

# Social Media Posting Workflow

Reference for how APR social/LinkedIn content gets drafted, where past topics live, and what decides which blog posts go into the next round. The moving parts live in the `agile-pain-relief-astro` and `social-media-posting` repos, not the vault.

## 1. Skills for drafting and posting

The seam is **Markdown in Obsidian → JSON in the repo**. You review and select Markdown; the JSON is a compile target you don't eyeball.

- **`linkedin-style`** (`Skills/APR/linkedin-style/SKILL.md`) - the human layer. **Draft mode** generates 2-3 LinkedIn-shaped options per item in your voice (reusing your own sentences), delivered in chat or a vault `*-drafts.md` file for you to review and pick. **Review mode** critiques an existing draft. It does not touch the JSON, character limits, or platform condensing.
- **`evergreen-posting`** (Astro repo: `.claude/skills/evergreen-posting/SKILL.md`) - the machine layer. Takes your selected drafts, condenses each to three platforms, threads the link where needed, and writes the batch JSON. Also drafts the AI Failure Modes quiz posts from seeds. It no longer counts characters or marks the calendar by hand: it calls `npm run validate`, and the scheduler stamps the calendar and quiz seeds itself.
- **`_social-posting-conventions.md`** (Astro repo) - the written-down version of limits, threading, hashtags, URL/UTM. Both skills cite it. It is documentation: **the pipeline code is the only implementation**, and `npm run validate` is how you check a file.
- **`social-media-adapt`** (Astro repo) - one-off: adapt a single LinkedIn post into Mastodon/Bluesky.
- **`criticmarkup-editing`** delivers voice critiques as inline suggestions when the draft is a Markdown file.
- `storybrand-messaging` / `Marketing/copy-editing` if the post leans promotional.

Realistic flow: `linkedin-style` draft mode (Markdown, you select) → `evergreen-posting` compiles the selected drafts to JSON → pipeline schedules.

## 2. Where past drafted topics live

- **Vault drafts:** `APR/Efforts/Social Media/` (filenames ending `-drafts` by convention). Currently `next-few-days-drafts.md` and `Surviving the AI Tsunami - Social Ideas.md`.
- **Pipeline batch JSON:** `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/` (written by `evergreen-posting`; the pipeline drains and refills `next-few-days.json`).
- **Posted history / prior promo language:** `analytics/history.json`, `history-archive.json`, `old_history.json` in the Astro repo. Grep a slug to find how a piece was promoted before, then mirror that angle/hashtags.

## 3. What decides which blog posts go into the next round

Governed by the **`evergreen-posting`** skill's "Content selection" rules, drawing from a curated queue:

- **Source of truth for blog posts:** `agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md`, specifically its **"Posting Queue"** section.
  - Skip anything marked `[x]` (already promoted).
  - Work the tiers in order: **TIER 1** (GenAI / supports the webinar) → **TIER 2** (proven traffic drivers) → **TIER 3** (Scrum & leadership staples).
- **Quiz hooks:** `social-media/planning/AI Failure Modes Quiz Generated Posts.md` (skip blocks marked `[POSTED YYYY-MM-DD]`).
- **Default cadence:** 2 posts/weekday (10:00 and 13:30 ET) = 1 quiz + 1 blog/glossary, interleaved so a day isn't all one theme. The slot count is defined in code (`social-media-posting/buffer-post/slotPlan.mjs`); that file is the authority if any doc says otherwise.
- **Queue hygiene:** `npm run calendar-audit` (in `social-media-posting`) diffs the reshare queue against the live blog/glossary so it doesn't drift from what's actually published.
- **Posted tracking is automatic:** `npm run batch` flips `- [ ]` to `- [x] (date)` and stamps `[POSTED date]` on the quiz seed as each post is accepted by Buffer. Nothing to mark by hand.

Short version: the **Posting Queue in `complete-social-media-calendar.md`** decides *which* posts are eligible and in what priority. Those tier/skip rules are applied at **draft time** (when `linkedin-style` drafts the blog/glossary/newsletter Markdown you select) and by **`evergreen-posting`** for quiz seeds and the compile + tracking.

## Key paths

- Astro repo: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro`
- Posting pipeline repo: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/social-media-posting`
- Shared authoring conventions: `agile-pain-relief-astro/.claude/skills/_social-posting-conventions.md`

28	
29	```
30	Update the social media reshare queue with recently published content.
31	
32	1. cd to /Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro
33	2. Run `npm run calendar-audit -- --verbose` to see what's live but not in the queue.
34	3. Find blog posts and glossary entries published since the last time I curated
35	   (check publish dates from the `date:` frontmatter field; sort newest first).
36	   Only surface items NOT already in complete-social-media-calendar.md.
37	4. Propose where each new item goes by tier:
38	   - GenAI / AI content -> TIER 1 (GenAI Content, or GenAI-Related Glossary)
39	   - High-search proven traffic pages -> TIER 2
40	   - Everything else Scrum/Agile -> TIER 3 (blog or glossary section)
41	   Show me the list with dates and proposed tiers, and ask before editing.
42	5. After I approve, add them as unposted `- [ ]` lines in the right sections,
43	   then run `npm run calendar-audit -- --write` to refresh the header counts.
44	```

47	
48	- The `date:` frontmatter is the publish date; `lastUpdated:` is a refresh and should be ignored for "recently published."
49	- New items go in as `- [ ]` (unposted). The `(YYYY-MM-DD)` suffix is only for posted `[x]` items.
50	- If you want a fresh, strategically important post (e.g. a new GenAI piece) reshared soon, tell Claude to place it near the **top** of its tier, not the bottom.
51	- Leave the edits unstaged for your normal commit flow.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Quarterly major update
56	
57	Re-tiers the queue based on performance. Uses the `apr-reshare-queue-tune` skill. Do the data refresh first (or confirm this week's Monday pull already ran).
58

60	
61	```
62	Run the quarterly reshare queue tune (apr-reshare-queue-tune skill).
63

65	   days, run it (scrapes social metrics into history.json, runs posthog-export).
66	2. Run `npm run reshare-report` from the astro repo root and read the table.
67	   It does the measurement: latest-snapshot dedup, LinkedIn-weighted clicks,
68	   times-reshared, clicks-per-reshare, engagement, low-confidence flags.
69	   Do NOT hand-compute any of this or write an inline script for it.
70	3. Rank and propose tier moves:
71	   - Top performers not in TIER 1/2 -> promote to TIER 2.
72	   - Duds (many reshares, near-zero clicks AND weak engagement) -> demote to bottom
73	     of tier, or retire to a "Rested" list (don't hard-delete).
74	   - Keep TIER 1 GenAI in TIER 1 regardless; flag weak ones for a hook rewrite.
75	   - Scan pageviews CSV + Ahrefs top pages for high-traffic pages NOT in the queue
76	     and propose adding them.
77	4. Guard against false signals: ignore low-confidence rows, weight steady LinkedIn
78	   over a one-off Mastodon spike, and check whether a zero-click item was simply
79	   not reshared inside the report's 30-day window.
80	5. Show me the ranked table + proposed moves and WAIT for approval (batch edit).
81	6. After I approve, edit complete-social-media-calendar.md (move the lines between
82	   tiers, keep posted markers), then run `npm run calendar-audit -- --write`.
83	```

85	### Notes

87	- The gold signal is `utm_campaign=archive-reshare` in `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` - it attributes site visits directly to reshares, per page per platform.
88	- Rank on **clicks-per-reshare**, never raw sessions (raw sessions just reward whatever was posted most recently / most often). `npm run reshare-report` already does this.
89	- LinkedIn is the main audience; a Mastodon-only bump is weak evidence.
90	- The measurement is code (`social-media-posting/reshare-report/`, with tests). The skill covers the judgement: which items move tier. If the two ever disagree, the code is right.
91	- The full method lives in the skill: `Skills/APR/reshare-queue-tune/SKILL.md`.
92	- Leave the edits unstaged for your normal commit flow.

# Social Media Posting Workflow

How APR social content gets drafted, scheduled, and how the reshare queue is kept healthy. The moving parts live in the `agile-pain-relief-astro` and `social-media-posting` repos, not the vault.

**Ground rule: anything the code does is not documented here.** Character limits, style rules, posted-marker syntax, slot cadence, and the reshare arithmetic all live in `social-media-posting` with tests, and are reached through `npm run` commands. This note covers the judgement calls and the running order. If a number appears in both places, the code is right and this note is stale.

## 1. The seam

**Markdown in Obsidian → JSON in the repo.** You review and select Markdown; the JSON is a compile target you don't eyeball.

`linkedin-style` draft mode (Markdown, you select) → `evergreen-posting` compiles to JSON → `npm run validate` → `npm run batch` schedules and marks the sources.

- **`linkedin-style`** (`Skills/APR/linkedin-style/SKILL.md`) - the human layer. Draft mode generates 2-3 LinkedIn-shaped options per item in your voice; review mode critiques an existing draft. Does not touch JSON, limits, or condensing.
- **`evergreen-posting`** (Astro repo) - the machine layer. Compiles selected drafts into batch JSON across three platforms, threading the link where it won't fit. Also drafts the AI Failure Modes quiz posts from seeds.
- **`social-media-adapt`** (Astro repo) - one-off: adapt a single LinkedIn post into Mastodon/Bluesky.
- **`_social-posting-conventions.md`** (Astro repo) - authoring judgement only: emoji, tone, hashtag choice, sourcing, and the character budgets to write within. The rules themselves are enforced by `npm run validate`.
- **`criticmarkup-editing`** for inline voice critiques on a Markdown draft; `storybrand-messaging` / `Marketing/copy-editing` if a post leans promotional.

## 2. Where drafts and history live

- **Vault drafts:** `APR/Efforts/Social Media/`, filenames ending `-drafts`.
- **Batch JSON:** `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/` (the pipeline drains and refills `next-few-days.json`).
- **Prior promo language:** `analytics/history.json`, `history-archive.json`, `old_history.json`. Grep a slug to see how a piece was promoted before, then mirror the angle.

## 3. What goes into the next batch

The **Posting Queue** in `social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md` decides what's eligible and in what order. This part is judgement and stays here:

- Skip anything already marked `[x]`.
- Work the tiers in order: **TIER 1** (GenAI / supports the webinar) → **TIER 2** (proven traffic drivers) → **TIER 3** (Scrum & leadership staples).
- Quiz hooks come from `social-media/planning/AI Failure Modes Quiz Generated Posts.md`; skip blocks already marked posted.
- Interleave so a day isn't all one theme.

For how many posts a day, read the header of the calendar file: it is regenerated by `npm run calendar-audit -- --write` from the scheduler's own slot plan, so it can't drift. Don't write the number down anywhere else; it has been wrong in three places before.

**Posted tracking is automatic.** `npm run batch` marks the calendar and the quiz seed as each post is accepted by Buffer. Nothing to mark by hand, and nothing to un-mark unless you delete a post from Buffer afterwards.

Two jobs, two cadences. Copy the prompt into Claude Code.

| Update | Cadence | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Minor** | Monthly (fold into the GSC export sitting) | Add newly published posts / glossary entries to the queue |
| **Major** | Quarterly (fold into the quarterly review) | Re-tier by what actually drives clicks, via `apr-reshare-queue-tune` |

- Astro repo: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro`
- Posting pipeline: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/social-media-posting`

## Commands (all run from the Astro repo root)

| Command | Does |

| `npm run validate` | Pre-flight `social-media/temp/` (single post) |
